newsitem.title: CANADA: Cargill's Alberta beef plant workers set to vote.
newsitem.headline: Cargill's Alberta beef plant workers set to vote.

text.p: Cargill Ltd's 1,600 striking Alberta beef plant employees were set to vote on a tentative labor contract on Friday, Cargill vice president Barb Isman said.
"They reached a tentative agreement yesterday and they're voting on it late this afternoon and this evening," she said.
The Calgary Herald newspaper reported that the United Food and Commercial Workers' union recommended to its members they vote in favor of the offer.
Isman would not discuss the specifics of the agreement.
Workers had previously rejected Cargill's offer of a graduated C$1.50 an hour raise over four years.
The UFCW sought C$1.95 over three years.
The plant, one of Canada's largest, usually slaughters 4,000 head of cattle a day.
Voting ends at 2100 MDT, Isman said.
Cargill Ltd is a unit of Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc.
